title: O JESUS, Let Thy Dying Cry
description: O JESUS, Let Thy Dying Cry in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 341.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O JE-SUS, let thy dy-ing cry Pierce to the bot-tom of my heart, Its e-vils cure, its wants sup-ply, And bid my un-be-lief de-part.

lines: O JESUS, let thy dying cry
Pierce to the bottom of my heart,
Its evils cure, its wants supply,
Slay the dire root and seed of sin;
Prepare for thee the holiest place;
Then, O essential Love, come in!
And fill thy house with endless praise.
Let me, according to thy word,
Which grieves at having grieved its Lord,
A heart thy joys and griefs to feel,
A heart that cannot faithless prove,
A heart where Christ alone may dwell,
All praise, all meekness, and all love.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
